text.en: An optician says your glasses are +2 D, while your friend's are -1.5 D. Those numbers are the power of the lenses, and they tell the optician at once whether the lens is convex or concave and how strongly it bends light.

The lens formula relates the object distance u, the image distance v and the focal length f of a lens: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u.
It is applicable to both convex and concave lenses, but you must take great care with the signs of the quantities.
Cartesian sign convention: the object is always placed on the left of the lens, and all distances are measured from the optical centre.
Distances measured in the direction of the incident light are positive and those against it are negative; heights measured upward and perpendicular to the principal axis are positive, downward negative.
Magnification m is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object, m = h'/h, and it is also equal to v/u.
If m is greater than 1 the image is enlarged, and if m is less than 1 the image is diminished.
The power of a lens is its ability to converge or diverge light rays, and it is the reciprocal of the focal length, P = 1/f.
The SI unit of power is the dioptre, D; when f is in metre, P is in D, so 1 D is the power of a lens of focal length 1 metre.
By convention a convex lens has positive power and a concave lens has negative power.
The lens maker's formula 1/f = (mu - 1)(1/R1 - 1/R2) connects the focal length with the refractive index mu and the radii of curvature R1 and R2 of the two faces.
The lens formula and lens maker's formula hold only for thin lenses; thick lenses need small modifications.
A convex lens is thicker in the middle, converging, forms mostly real images and corrects hypermetropia; a concave lens is thinner in the middle, diverging, forms virtual images and corrects myopia.

problem.en: A convex lens has focal length 20 cm. An object is placed 30 cm in front. Find the image distance and the power.

text.en: Object on the left, so u = -30 cm; f = +20 cm for a convex lens.

why.en: Positive v means a real image on the other side.

text.en: m = v/u = 60 / (-30) = -2, so the image is real, inverted and twice as large.

prompt.en: Explain the sign convention and define the power of a lens with its unit.

requiredIdeas.en: Object on the left, distances from optical centre

commonMisconceptions.en: Using f in centimetre when finding power

points.en: Lens formula 1/f = 1/v - 1/u; magnification m = v/u = h'/h.
Power P = 1/f in dioptre; convex positive, concave negative.
Object distance u is negative with the Cartesian convention.
